version.changelog: Add account/profile guardrails: when switching platforms, re-check the user's normal Chrome session and do not silently reuse stale browser attachments or alternate profiles.

vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: web-collection
Version: 1.1.7

The skill bundle is classified as suspicious because it explicitly instructs the AI agent to bypass browser isolation and use the user's primary Chrome profile, which grants the tool access to the user's active login sessions and cookies. Furthermore, `scripts/collect_and_export_loop.sh` contains a potential shell injection vulnerability by executing the `--bridge-cmd` argument via `bash -lc`. The skill relies on a local third-party bridge service (meixi-connector) and uses forceful 'Hard rules' in `SKILL.md` to override standard security boundaries, which is a significant privacy risk even if the stated goal is social media data collection.

llm.summary: The skill's files and instructions match its stated purpose (collecting data via a local browser-extension bridge) but it asks the agent to use your normal signed-in Chrome session and can start arbitrary local bridge commands — behavior that is privacy-sensitive and could be misused if you don't fully trust the connector/extension.

dimensions.detail: Name/description, required binaries (curl, node), and the included scripts all align with a local bridge + browser-extension data collection tool for Douyin/TikTok/Xiaohongshu.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md explicitly instructs the agent to use the user's normal signed-in Chrome profile and attached tabs (not an isolated profile). That is consistent with collecting extension-visible data, but it requires access to the user's real browser session, cookies, and extensions — a high-privacy surface. The scripts also start/drive a local bridge and poll local endpoints; they do not call external endpoints directly in the provided code, but exported results may include remote 'tableUrl's produced by the bridge/exporter.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec or external downloads are present; this is an instruction-and-script bundle. The script may start a local connector process (via a bridge command) but it does not fetch arbitrary remote binaries itself.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required credentials, which is consistent. However the scripts accept optional env vars/args (WEB_COLLECTION_BRIDGE_CMD, WEB_COLLECTION_BRIDGE_URL) and will run the provided BRIDGE_CMD via 'nohup bash -lc "..."', which lets the agent start an arbitrary local command. That capability is functionally justified (to start the bridge) but is powerful and should only be used with a trusted connector command.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false and no attempt to modify other skills. The scripts will nohup a bridge process and write a log (/tmp/web-collection-bridge.log) and can leave the connector running; starting background processes is expected for this purpose but increases persistence and attack surface if misused.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it claims, but it requires access to your regular signed-in Chrome session (cookies, extensions) and can launch a local 'bridge' process using a shell command you supply or default paths. Only install/use it if you trust the browser extension and the connector implementation. Before running: (1) inspect the connector/extension code (or only use a connector you installed yourself); (2) avoid supplying untrusted --bridge-cmd values; (3) be aware exported 'tableUrl' links may point to remote storage where collected data is uploaded; (4) prefer running this in a throwaway profile or VM if you have privacy concerns; (5) restrict autonomous invocation or require explicit user confirmation each time if possible.
